correctness.rationale: Finite complete enumeration has an exact closure criterion: simultaneous unique-white-neighbor additions agree with sequential zero forcing; bit masks exhaust all 18- and 20-vertex subsets through sizes 7 and 8. Independently implemented sequential/parallel checks on the stated 9-line Pappus configuration and GP(10,3) Desargues graph found Z(P)=7 with 6912 sets and Z(D)=8 with 13520. Exact one-edge slides gave Pappus 10962 edges, degree classes 1080/3564/2268 of degrees 2/3/4, and Desargues zero edges. Full BFS from every Pappus state gave connected graph radius 16, diameter 18 and eccentricity counts 648/4968/1296; unrestricted Desargues jumps gave 178560 edges. Each enumeration is on a rigorously bounded set; finite exhaustive calculation is valid here, not extrapolated.

evidence: Previously published Z(D)=8 for GP(10,3); general zero-forcing upper/lower bounds provide a scalar cardinality.
The theorem additionally gives counts of all minima, exact local transition graphs and Pappus metric.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The strongest identified graph-family forcing-number theorem does not imply this configuration-space enumeration; a bound on optimum cannot determine local transitions.

value.rationale: Natural comparison of the classical Pappus and Desargues cubic bipartite girth-six incidence graphs isolates a sharp structural distinction: one entire minimum zero-forcing configuration space is mobile under local slides while the other is frozen despite a connected jump space. Exact full state reconfiguration and distance census is a nontrivial finite invariant useful as a benchmark and structural counterexample, rather than a trivial recomputation of Z(D)=8.
